bullets.title: Iran conflict drives oil above $97-100, inflation re-accelerating toward 3.76% in Q4
bullets.body: US-Iran hostilities escalated sharply this week — Iran launched electro-optical missiles at US warships, Houthis seized Yemen's Mokha port near Bab el-Mandeb, and Trump advisers now say war likely extends past Jan 2029. WTI at $97.40-97.65 (+0.8-1%), Brent crossed $100/bbl; Hedgeye's US Inflation Nowcast re-accelerating from 3.36% in July to 3.76% in Q4 2026. Primary inflation driver has shifted from crude to diesel, freight, and refined product scarcity.

bullets.title: 10yr yield at 4.86% — new cycle high; 62-63% probability of Sep 16 Fed hike
bullets.body: UST 10yr hit 4.86% (highest since Oct 2023); UST 2yr at 4.44% — both new inflation cycle highs. Bond market pricing ~62-63% probability of a 25bp hike at the Sep 16 FOMC. Friday's August CPI is the pivotal data point: JPM's Feroli models Core MoM +0.21%; a 0.2% rounded print supports a hold, a 0.3% print supports a hike. Equity Risk Premia compressed to ~2%, 100bp below historical avg, amplifying yield sensitivity.

bullets.title: Market breadth deteriorating sharply since Aug 14; correction anatomy worsening
bullets.body: NYSE Cumulative Breadth peaked Aug 14 and has been negative ~2/3 of the subsequent 18 trading days; NYSE/NASDAQ New Highs minus New Lows also negative ~60-67% of sessions. Over 80% of S&P 500 constituents were down Wednesday, averaging -1.5%. Sector declines QTD: Industrials -8%, Utilities -5.3%, Consumer Disc. -4%, Real Estate -4%; Healthcare is the outlier at +5% QTD.

bullets.title: TSMC August revenue +53% YoY to record; AI datacenter demand visible to 2029-30
bullets.body: TSMC August revenue came in at NT$514.8B (+53% YoY, +10% MoM), tracking the mid-to-high end of Q3 guidance. N3 supply shortage is expected to worsen; datacenter AI demand visibility extends to 2029-30 with order books already full for 2028. TSMC's 1.4nm fab in Taichung may reach mass production by 2027, ahead of the 2028 plan.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades META to OW at $820 PT on Muse AI agent traction and Watermelon model
bullets.body: JPMorgan (Anmuth) upgraded META from Neutral to Overweight, raising PT from $640 to $820 (23x 2028E GAAP EPS of $35.44). Muse AI agent hit #3 on US App Store day 2, with usage running 10x above testing cohorts; next-gen Watermelon model described as significantly more advanced. Wells Fargo also upgraded META to Overweight citing frontier AI products beyond ads; Street now stands at 72 buys, 7 holds, 0 sells.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler initiates AI compute sector; models 5x compute market growth to $2.2T by 2030
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiated 7 AI compute names with top OW picks on AVGO ($460 PT), NVDA ($300 PT), AMD ($600 PT), and ARM ($320 PT); INTC and QBTS rated Neutral, MRVL OW into Oct 6 analyst day. Piper's thesis: compute market grows 5x to $2.2T by 2030, driving ~45% EPS CAGR for compute enablers; 2027 capacity already sold out, order books full for 2028.

bullets.title: DOJ probes Nvidia's $17B Groq licensing deal for antitrust circumvention
bullets.body: The DOJ is investigating whether Nvidia's $17B licensing deal with Groq was structured to circumvent antitrust review. This follows elevated regulatory scrutiny on AI infrastructure consolidation and adds headline risk to NVDA despite broadly bullish street sentiment and fresh Piper Sandler OW initiation.

bullets.title: Rising yields + oil pressuring Consumer Discretionary and homebuilders technically
bullets.body: XLY Technical Score 2/10, sitting below both 50- and 200-day MAs with downside target of 105 from 114.71; 59% of Consumer Disc. stocks rated Weak/Poor. XHB (homebuilders) Technical Score 0/10 with 100% of constituents below 50-day MA and downside target of 85. The framework: rising oil and yields are directly biting cyclical demand-sensitive sectors.

bullets.title: 22V: Long Value factor as 10yr above 4.75% restrictive threshold; Value-Momentum blend best hedge
bullets.body: 22V Research flags that 10yr yields above 4.75% are restrictive to risk-on factors and non-AI cyclicals; fair value estimated at 4.5% with yields likely staying elevated as inflation risk remains. Value factor has shown consistent positive monthly returns under current macro regime; a Value+Momentum blend is up 9% YTD and dampens vol without sacrificing upside. Low Vol requires a worse economic backdrop to work longer-term.

bullets.title: Factor regime: Hedgeye downgrades RUT and AMZN to Bearish; SPX and NASDAQ still Bullish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's 9/10 Risk Range signals: Russell 2000 (IWM) moved from Neutral to Bearish; AMZN downgraded to Bearish; TSLA upgraded from Bearish to Neutral. MSFT, AAPL, META, NVDA, SNOW remain Bullish. SPX risk range 7601-7757; COMPQ 26,014-26,683. Small-cap and broad market internals deteriorating even as mega-cap tech holds.

bullets.title: ECB hiking 25bp today to 2.65%; BOJ expected at 1.25% next week — global tightening continues
bullets.body: The ECB is expected to hike +25bps to 2.65% today; the BOJ is expected to hike to 1.25% next week with policy rate potentially reaching 1.75% sooner than previously forecast. JPM's international desk notes EUR 1Y1Y may decouple from TTF despite limited second-round inflation effects. Sovereign bond yields rising in Asia and Europe in tandem with US on geopolitical tensions.

bullets.title: ORCL and ADBE report tonight — key AI monetization reads for the tape
bullets.body: ORCL reports after close with 11% implied move; Street expects FQ1 IaaS in mid-to-high 110s% YoY vs guidance of 57-63% Cloud CC growth; short interest near multi-year highs. ADBE also reports tonight (EPS est. $6.08, rev $6.69B) — stock is -26% YTD with ARR organic growth guidance already cut from ~10% to ~8% due to AI pricing deflation; OpenAI banning competing AI ads in ChatGPT adds additional headwind for ADBE.

bullets.title: Apple iPhone 18 event: foldable Duo at $1,999 impressed; Pro $100 price hike below fears
bullets.body: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo foldable at $1,999 (lower than feared) and iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max at $1,199/$1,299 (+$100 YoY, also below worst-case estimates). Street reaction is in-line to slightly positive; supply on Duo limited to 8-10M units due to yield/capacity constraints. MS notes 57% of iPhone base is >4 years old, supporting upgrade cycle; Jefferies cautions Apple is pursuing volume-over-margin strategy.

bullets.title: MRVL CEO flags societal pushback risk on data center builds; AI infra stocks selling off
bullets.body: MRVL CEO Matt Murphy noted suppliers are growing nervous about societal resistance to new data center construction — commentary that coincided with a broad selloff in AI infrastructure stocks. CRWV -3.8%, NBIS -3.8%, AXTI -3.5%, ALAB -2.8% in premarket. Despite the tone, MRVL CEO separately raised the company's revenue outlook by $10B to $30B with datacenter at $15-16B next year.

bullets.title: August ad checks strong for NFLX, ROKU, YouTube, PINS; TikTok and TTD weakest
bullets.body: Piper's August ad checks show NFLX, ROKU, YouTube, and PINS outperforming vs. expectations; TikTok, TTD, and SNAP were weakest. ChatGPT Ads crossed $1B ARR by August (from ~600 to 10,000+ advertisers in 7 months) but ROI perception remains middling — on par with Pinterest, well below Google and Instagram. Pinterest is the only major platform where agencies plan to cut spend in both 2026 and 2027.

bullets.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash cuts inference costs 70-98% vs competitors — AI model commoditization accelerating
bullets.body: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash using a Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture that reduces HBM and SSD requirements to 1/4 and 1/8 of prior model via KV cache compression. Peak-hour pricing is 87%/78%/70% cheaper than DS-V4-Pro and 98%/90%/92% cheaper than Kimi-K3. Enterprise AI adoption spending already slowed in August with top 1% AI users cutting spending nearly 10% as customers shift to older, cheaper models.

bullets.title: JPM: Tactically Cautious/Neutral; favor Mag7, Software, Large-Cap Banks into CPI
bullets.body: JPM market intelligence is Tactically Cautious/Neutral heading into Friday CPI. A dovish core MoM print (0.2%) would benefit Momentum/Tech/Cyclicals; a hot 0.3% print supports a hike. Preferred plays: Mag7, Software (attractive if Semis weaken), Large-Cap Banks, and Consumer Discretionary if energy declines. Treasury 10Y auction stopped 1.5bp through, largest through result since April 2025, suggesting demand at current yields.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers +12% QTD vs Semiconductor basket -23%; semis need positive re-rating catalyst
bullets.body: Citi's hyperscaler basket (CGUSHYPR) is up 12% QTD while the semiconductor basket (CGUSSEMI) is down 23%. Semi-cap equipment needs $215B+ WFE and foundry/logic updates to reignite; analog semis need a better AI narrative to break out of auto/industrial cycle. Investors at Citi TMT dinner prefer networking/optical exposure (LITE, MRVL, COHR) over memory, analog, and semi-cap.

bullets.title: September macro calendar: CPI (9/11), FOMC (9/16), Trump-Xi meeting (9/24) are key inflection points
bullets.body: Options market implies +/-74-82bps SPX moves around these events. SPX 1M implied vol is near multi-year lows at 12, creating attractive short-term vol buying opportunities per Citi. ORCL (tonight) and MU (9/30) are the critical AI earnings gauges before October earnings season begins.

bullets.title: Copper -3% on White House stalling refined copper tariffs; Middle East geopolitical risk premium broadening
bullets.body: The White House is stalling on refined copper tariffs due to competing pressures on domestic mining benefits vs. manufacturing input costs; copper fell 3% (two standard deviations) on the report. South Korea reportedly nearing a $100B+ US energy investment commitment including up to eight nuclear plants for AI build-out. Materials sector momentum has stalled after the early-year rally with post-peak inflation and no significant easing before 2027.
